title: A Buddha made of snow
translation: Look at what people keep themselves busy with. It's like making a Buddha out of snow on a spring day, ordering gold, silver and jewels to decorate it, and starting work on a temple to put it in. Will it last until the temple is ready, so you can set it up inside?
You think your life is solid. Meanwhile it's melting from underneath, like the snow, and you're still making plans and waiting for them to be finished.
original: {人間|にんげん}の{営|いとな}みあへる{業|わざ}を{見|み}るに、{春|はる}の{日|ひ}に{雪仏|ゆきぼとけ}を{造|つく}りて、その{為|ため}に{金銀|きんぎん}{珠玉|しゆぎよく}の{飾|かざ}りを{営|いとな}み、{堂塔|だうたふ}を{建|た}てむとするに{似|に}たり。
その{構|かま}へを{待|ま}ちてよく{安置|あんち}してむや。
{人|ひと}の{命|いのち}ありと{見|み}る{程|ほど}も、{下|した}より{消|き}ゆる{事|こと}、{雪|ゆき}の{如|ごと}くなるうちに、いとなみ{待|ま}つこと{甚|はなは}だ{多|おほ}し。
literal: Looking at the work people busy themselves with, it is like making a snow Buddha on a spring day, preparing decorations of gold, silver and jewels for it, and trying to build a hall and pagoda.
Will one wait for the building and properly enshrine it?
Even while one sees that a person's life is there, it melts away from below like snow, and meanwhile the things one prepares and waits for are very many.

notes.text: {雪仏|ゆきぼとけ}: a Buddha made of snow. It is a spring day, so the snow is already melting.
{堂塔|だうたふ}: the halls and pagodas of a temple. Building a hall for a Buddha image was a large, expensive project that could take years.
{構|かま}へ: the building work (the 1925 edition glosses it 'construction').
{安置|あんち}: to set up a Buddha image in its hall. てむや: 'will it surely…?', a rhetorical question. It will not.
Snow in spring melts from below, where you cannot see it, and looks solid until it gives way. The reading した for 下 is the edition's.

いとなむ is the same word as {営|いとな}み at the start of the section: 'to busy oneself, to work on something'. The edition glosses いとなみ{待|ま}つ as 'to plan something and wait for it to be finished'. So the section ends where it began, with the busy work.
